name: Masculism
summary: Masculism is a loosely defined current that treats men as a sex facing systematic disadvantages, in areas such as conscription, custody, suicide, health and schooling, and rejects the claim that men as a group hold power over women. Its mainstream, represented by Warren Farrell, wants gender liberation for both sexes, but writers also use the term for antifeminism or the promotion of masculine ideals.
scope: The progressive or egalitarian masculist strand of Warren Farrell, Ferrel Christensen and the men's movement, as described on Wikipedia and in Farrell's own writing. It excludes the male-supremacist 'extremist' strand and the Christian Mighty Men movements, which differ on gender roles. Masculism has no doctrine outside gender, family and conscription issues, so most answers on other topics are neutral and low-confidence.

sources.usedFor: Farrell's trajectory and claims on conscription, suicide, domestic violence, pay gap and affirmative action.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Farrell cites men's shorter life spans and health neglect, but no masculist source states a view on universal healthcare.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage floors are not a masculist issue and adherents range across economic views.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Economic organisation is outside masculism; Farrell's pay analysis uses market choices but does not defend markets generally.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax levels on the rich are outside masculism's gender focus.

unions-good.rationale: Farrell stresses that men fill the most dangerous jobs and most workplace deaths, but neither he nor the masculism literature says whether unions help; no answer can be drawn from that.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Masculist writing targets courts, the draft and health spending, not business regulation, and adherents run from libertarian to left on economics.

cut-welfare.rationale: Farrell criticises the expectation that men earn and provide, but no masculist source takes a side on cutting welfare programmes as such.

worker-ownership.rationale: Masculist sources discuss men's paid work only as a burden of the provider role; collective ownership of firms is never raised.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Counter-terrorism surveillance is not a masculist concern and adherents hold varied civil-liberties views.

rehabilitation.rationale: Masculists object to sentencing disparities for men but have no stated view on prison purpose.

traditional-family.rationale: Adherents split between the mythopoetic and Christian masculinist strands that favour traditional families and the progressive strand that wants flexible roles.

abortion-legal.rationale: Masculism raises men's lack of say over fatherhood but has no settled position on whether abortion should be legal.

more-religion-public.rationale: Christian masculinist groups such as Mighty Men want more religion in public life while the progressive strand is secular, so no common view.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Farrell stresses socialisation into rigid roles (men as success objects), but also treats some sex differences as real, and the traditionalist strand grounds roles in nature.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration levels never come up in Farrell's work or the Wikipedia overview of masculism, whose issues are custody, conscription, violence and health.

open-borders.rationale: No masculist text addresses border policy; the movement's grievances concern family courts and male-only obligations within a country.

limit-growth.rationale: Farrell compares neglect of men's health to ignoring global warming, but only as an analogy; masculists take no view on limiting growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate appears in Farrell only as a metaphor for interconnection between the sexes, which gives no basis for a policy answer.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy, including nuclear power, is absent from Farrell's writing and from accounts of masculism.

experts-over-public.rationale: Masculists distrust academic experts in gender studies, but there is no general stance on expert rule.

central-planning.rationale: Masculist sources do not compare planned and market economies; adherents are found on both left and right.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Distributist ideas about property ownership are absent from masculist writing.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Farrell discusses pay as a trade-off that people choose, not something to abolish.

workers-councils.rationale: Council-based government is foreign to the masculism literature, which works through existing democratic institutions.

right-to-secede.rationale: No masculist source addresses regional secession.

war-builds-character.rationale: Farrell treats war as the clearest case of men being expendable and told it is glory, so he would deny it is good for a nation's character.

separate-church-state.rationale: Christian masculinist and secular strands differ, so adherents are split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Christian masculinist movements might say yes while the progressive strand would say no, so adherents split.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Masculists want to reform public family courts, not privatise courts, but take no stance on the principle.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Ethnic composition of the nation is unrelated to masculism and its adherents hold varied views.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Farrell attributes pay gaps to life choices rather than discrimination, implying equal outcomes are not a proper goal.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land rights are not among the issues listed for masculism in Farrell's work or the reference overview.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Farrell argues men are taught self-sacrifice as protectors, yet he frames the fix as mutual interdependence ('when either sex wins, both lose') rather than an ethic of self-interest; no clear answer follows.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy does not appear in masculist sources.

algorithmic-government.rationale: No masculist source discusses algorithms or AI in government.

restore-past-order.rationale: Traditionalist masculinism wants to restore a lost order, while the progressive strand rejects that.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Farrell relies on outcome data but masculism has no stated stance on pragmatic policy judgement.

direct-action.rationale: Masculist groups use lobbying, protest and conferences, but there is no stated rule against elections.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Farrell says men trade power and health for pay as a choice, not as exploitation by owners, but there is no stated view on profit.

collective-farming.rationale: Agricultural organisation is absent from masculist writing.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Farrell condemns that men are the ones sent to die in war but does not trace war to capitalism or any economic system.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Masculists claim men as a group are disadvantaged, which is a group-rights style claim, yet they stress equal treatment of individuals.

exit-over-voice.rationale: No masculist source compares emigration and voting as checks on government.

positive-liberty.rationale: Farrell defines power as control over one's own life, which is close to a positive-liberty idea, but he applies it to gender roles only and takes no position on material guarantees.

national-rebirth.rationale: Davidson's virism blames decline in masculine values, but it is one thinker's view and not shared by the progressive strand.

single-common-good.rationale: Masculism frames itself as advocating for one sex's interests, but has no stated view on a unitary common good.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora citizenship is not a masculist issue in any source.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is absent from the masculism literature.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporate governance and worker votes do not feature in masculist writing.

economic-freedom.rationale: No masculist source links political and economic freedom; adherents span economic ideologies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Mythopoetic and evangelical strands appeal to myth and faith while Farrell appeals to data, so adherents differ.

class-collaboration.rationale: Farrell rejects a zero-sum struggle between the sexes, but neither he nor other masculists apply that to employers and workers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural institutions and futurist views of heritage are outside anything masculist sources discuss.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Fossil-fuel production is not a masculist issue in any source, though Farrell notes men do most mining and oil work as hazardous jobs.

elite-replacement.rationale: Outside masculism, though masculists claim elites favour women, a different claim.

national-mission.rationale: No masculist source speaks of a national mission to spread a form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Masculists deny that men as a group hold systematic power; Farrell calls male power largely a myth and masculist scholarship rejects universal patriarchy, though the male-supremacist strand sees male dominance as natural.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Farrell argues that powerful-looking men are not truly powerful, but masculists do not make a general populist claim about corrupt elites.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle slaughter laws have no connection to any masculist source.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Theories of the socialist state are absent from masculist writing.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Farrell ties rights to responsibilities (voting and draft registration), but no masculist source states a theory of political legitimacy.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional checks and balances are not a masculist topic; the movement criticises family courts' rulings, not their place in the constitution.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist party organisation is foreign to masculist writing.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Farrell notes that men are most of the homeless, but masculists do not argue that institutions should prioritise the poor generally.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law does not appear in the masculism literature.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection of officials by lot is not a masculist topic.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Legislators' pay is not a masculist issue in any source.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential term rules are outside anything masculists write about.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of elected officials is not a masculist topic.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Farrell objects to who is sent abroad to fight, not to alliances or overseas deployments as such, so no answer follows.

people-in-arms.rationale: No masculist stance on replacing professional armies; only the male-only burden of service is addressed.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Masculist writing does not compare rural and urban moral life; the mythopoetic strand's wilderness retreats are about male identity, not settlement.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Outside masculism, though masculists criticise gender-studies academics.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Masculist sources do not rank or compare cultures and civilizations.

death-penalty.rationale: Masculists complain that men receive harsher sentences, but there is no common view on capital punishment itself.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Masculists back gender equality teaching in principle but criticise school curricula as favouring girls, so adherents are split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: No settled masculist position; mythopoetic and Christian strands might favour limits while others value free expression.

minority-language-support.rationale: Minority language policy is not a masculist issue.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Decolonisation and economic transformation are outside masculist writing.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional rewriting is not a masculist topic.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Masculist sources do not weigh political freedom against development.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank governance is not a masculist topic.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy is not a masculist topic.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation and occupation law are outside masculist writing.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: State control of clergy is not a masculist topic in any source.

character-from-environment.rationale: Farrell attributes male behaviour largely to socialisation and father absence, an inference to the general claim.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is not a masculist topic.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is absent from masculist writing.

equal-parenting.rationale: Farrell's central custody claim is that children do best with about equal time with each parent, and he wants courts to presume shared time.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentist claims based on co-ethnics abroad are not a masculist topic.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-national unity of kin peoples is absent from masculist writing.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm bailouts are not a masculist topic.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Outside masculism, though masculists criticise family courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Farrell argues affirmative action increases inequality and that feminism favours women, so mandated equal representation of women is opposed as favouritism.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Guerrilla theory is entirely outside masculism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Farrell argues affirmative action increases inequality; extending that to race is an inference, not a documented masculist position.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not a masculist topic.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory trade policy is outside masculist writing.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaties are not a masculist topic.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty is not a masculist topic.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Outside masculism; Farrell questions men's duty to provide as a burden.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Male suicide, shorter life expectancy and boys' schooling problems are central masculist concerns, and no current statement asks about them.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Masculists assert gender symmetry in domestic violence and want services for abused men, as the Masculism and Farrell articles describe.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Outside masculism, and adherents range across economic views.

party-own-road.rationale: Relations between communist parties are outside masculist writing.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: No masculist source addresses foreign development.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Outside masculism's concerns and adherents are split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: No masculist source addresses this and adherents are split.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not a masculist issue; adherents are split.

filial-duty.rationale: Masculism has no stated view on filial duty; adherents are split.

office-by-exam.rationale: Recruitment of officials by examination is not a masculist topic.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Communal land tenure is not a masculist topic.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land ownership by foreigners is not a masculist topic.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about status seeking rather than the pursuit of possessions, which is what the statement now asks about.

reviewHistory.rationale: Farrell says men pursue earnings and status at the cost of time and health, but he frames this as a gender-role problem, not a critique of consumerism.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Intervention within military blocs is not a masculist topic.

residents-only-property.rationale: Property purchase rules are not a masculist issue and adherents range across views.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment guarantees are not a masculist issue, though Farrell notes men's concentration in dangerous jobs; adherents range across views.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democracy promotion is not a masculist issue and adherents range across views.

non-intervention.rationale: Foreign intervention is not a masculist issue and adherents range across views.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not a masculist issue and adherents range across views.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Farrell and the progressive strand seek shared parenting and equal custody rights within marriage and family law, not abolition of legal marriage, though men's movement critics of marriage law exist.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Government transparency is not a masculist issue and adherents range across views.

local-production.rationale: Local production is not a masculist issue and adherents range across views.

national-law-over-international.rationale: National versus international law is not a masculist issue and adherents range across views.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical or religious claims to land are not a masculist topic.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The mainstream strand, represented by Farrell, is a liberal egalitarian movement with no link to denial.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Farrell argues that men and women both face disadvantages and disputes the feminist claim that men as a group hold power over women.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Farrell describes himself as having moved across the spectrum and calls for gender liberation beyond the standard camps, but masculism makes no general claim.

alienated-labor.rationale: Farrell discusses men's work roles and burdens, but not alienation under capitalism.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules are not a masculist topic.

social-market-economy.rationale: Masculists do not choose between economic models; adherents range from libertarian to social democratic.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Masculists oppose male-only conscription, but that is a demand for equal duty or abolition of the draft, not abolition of the armed forces.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist banking is not a masculist topic.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Masculists deny that men as a group dominate women, and Farrell argues against the power-over-women premise this ecofeminist claim relies on.

reification.rationale: The Marxist theory of reification is absent from masculist writing.

racial-franchise.rationale: The progressive strand seeks equality for both sexes and has no racial exclusion; the scope excludes the male-supremacist strand.

open-government-data.rationale: Government transparency rules are not a masculist topic.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Masculism is not a religious doctrine; adherents are split between secular egalitarians and Christian traditionalists, so no stated position.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The ideology never addressed divided societies, and nothing in its principles points either way.

term-limits.rationale: No stated position; adherents are split and the issue lies outside gender, family and conscription.

vote-delegation.rationale: No stated position on democratic mechanisms; adherents are split.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Farrell's gender liberation involves flexible, shared roles for men and women in family life, including shared breadwinning and child-raising.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not a masculist topic.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Formal recognition of genocides is not a masculist topic, though some masculists point out that massacres often target men.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The sources state no position; Farrell criticises male conscription but is not pacifist on self-defence.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Masculism treats men and women as sex groups with distinct disadvantages, so it relies on fixed sex categories.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Only the evangelical masculinist groups bring religion in, and they speak of male headship, not politics as a cosmic struggle; the egalitarian sources are secular.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Cultural Zionist ideas of a homeland for a diaspora are outside masculist writing.

culture-before-state.rationale: The order of cultural and state building is not a masculist topic.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence from the state is not a masculist topic.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not a masculist issue; adherents range across economic views.

municipal-property.rationale: Ownership of the means of production is outside masculist concerns.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Farrell stresses men's health neglect, but no masculist source addresses drug approval.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Strands differ: Christian and mythopoetic strands emphasize the spiritual, the progressive mainstream does not.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The legal basis of regional self-government is not a masculist topic.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate religious electorates are not a masculist topic.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Secret versus open diplomacy is not a masculist topic.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Masculists criticize male-only conscription and treat men as disposable in war, but do not generally call for refusing all state wars.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Labor bargaining is not a masculist concern, and adherents are not united on it.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules lie outside the movement's concerns, and adherents hold varied economic views.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Exploitation of poorer regions within a state is not a masculist topic.

public-service-media.rationale: Public media funding is not a masculist issue, and adherents are split between those wary of media bias and others.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Masculism has no theology; its evangelical groups are Christian and its egalitarian authors secular, so they would not agree on religious pluralism.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Whether regional varieties form one language is not a masculist topic.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Masculism has no position on the environment, and adherents are split between libertarian and egalitarian leanings.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Union membership rules are not a masculist issue and adherents range across economic views.

voter-id.rationale: Voter identification is outside masculist concerns, which centre on gender, family and conscription.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is not a masculist issue and adherents range across economic views.

women-suffrage.rationale: The egalitarian masculist strand wants equal rights and equal accountability for both sexes, and does not contest women's vote; Farrell's argument is that equal rights should carry equal duties such as draft registration.

race-social-construct.rationale: Race is outside masculism's concerns, and adherents hold varied views.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: No masculist source discusses international criminal courts.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Defending bureaucratic planned states is outside masculist writing.

indirect-election.rationale: Council-based indirect elections are not a masculist topic.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Plebiscites over disputed territory are not a masculist topic.

simple-living.rationale: Farrell urges men to trade earning for time with family, friends and health, a gender-role point that stops short of endorsing simple or self-sufficient living.

equal-conscription.rationale: Farrell argues that registering and drafting only men is sex discrimination and that women should carry the same obligation, or the draft be dropped.

self-ownership.rationale: Farrell's objection to male-only conscription rests on men's right to decide about their own bodies and lives, which matches self-ownership.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: No masculist source takes a side on targeted versus universal social spending.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Religious denominations in politics are outside masculism's concerns, apart from the Christian Mighty Men strand which is excluded.

national-resource-control.rationale: National resource control is not a masculist topic.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Farrell criticises the expectation that men earn and provide, but no masculist source takes a side on cutting welfare programmes as such. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Boys and men facing disadvantage in education, health and suicide deserve the same public attention and programmes as girls and women.
missingStatements.rationale: Male suicide, shorter life expectancy and boys' schooling problems are central masculist concerns, and no current statement asks about them.

missingStatements.text: Domestic violence by women against men is as serious as violence by men against women and should receive equal services and protection.
missingStatements.rationale: Masculists assert gender symmetry in domestic violence and want services for abused men, as the Masculism and Farrell articles describe.

notes: Strands differ: the progressive strand seeks equality for both sexes, the mythopoetic and Christian strands favour distinct gender roles, and the extremist strand promotes male supremacy. Wikipedia notes the term is also used for antifeminism and machismo.
